title: The Black Bank Merger: M&F, Optus and a Rival Bid in Durham | Across the Water, Ep. 3
lede: Shareholders of Mechanics and Farmers Bank, founded in 1907 on Durham's Black Wall Street, vote on Nov 4 on a $105 million cash merger with Optus Bank of Columbia, South Carolina. This episode explains the deal, why both banks say they need scale, the rival bid from Greensboro's Triad Business Bank, and what the vote means for a sector that keeps shrinking.
keyPoints: Optus agreed in July to buy M&F for about $105 million in cash; the combined bank would hold about $1.27 billion in assets across 10 locations (Banking Dive, American Banker).
M&F's legal lending limit is $11 million; combined, the bank could lend about $20 million to one borrower (ABC11).
The Chicago Fed counted 33 Black-owned banks in 2010 and 21 in 2022; FDIC data cited by American Banker put the count at 17 this March. Counts vary by definition.
Triad Business Bank offers $53.50 a share in cash for up to 25% of shares, the rest in stock; Optus pays up to $53.30 in cash, $6.73 of it contingent. M&F's board unanimously backs Optus.
Meetings on Oct 7 and Oct 20 were adjourned; the vote reconvenes Nov 4 at 10 a.m. ET. The deal also needs federal approval.
